articles.title: Gap, American Eagle shares fall as brand troubles weaken forecasts
articles.summary:
STORY: Shares of Gap and American Eagle each plummeted on Friday, after both retailers issued weak sales forecasts, signaling deepening pressure on consumer discretionary spending.

Gap, which is in the midst of a turnaround, cut its sales forecast, while American Eagle kept its forecast intact but cautioned about near-term gross margins.

Shares of Gap tumbled as much as 18% in morning trading, while American Eagle fell nearly 19%.

Some analysts said the "key swing factor" pressuring sales at Gap was its Old Navy chain, where seasonal women's apparel, including dresses, failed to connect with shoppers.

:: Archive

Some women's apparel at American Eagle also faced challenges, despite strength at the company's Aerie sub-brand.

American Eagle recently launched another ad campaign with actor Sydney Sweeney to attract Gen Z shoppers, a year after a viral and controversial ad featuring Sweeney fueled a stock rally.

But analysts at Barclays cautioned that repeating last year's success may be difficult, even as the company continues to spend on marketing in the current quarter.

The results at both retailers underscore a widening split in consumer spending, with record-low sentiment driven by the Iran war forcing lower-income households to cut back amid higher gas prices.

Higher-income shoppers, however, remain selectively willing to treat themselves to certain clothing or beauty items.

Earlier this week, Abercrombie & Fitch and Bath & Body Works posted strong quarterly results, indicating continued appetite for those affordable indulgences.
